key_insight: A polynomial-time classical algorithm can efficiently simulate single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits and match or beat the energy results of large quantum chemistry experiments.
engineering_relevance: This shows that some near-term quantum chemistry workloads may be classically reproducible, making fast simulators and circuit optimization important for benchmarking and resource planning.
method: Derive a polynomial-time simulation method for any single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuit.
Use the simulator to compute ground-state energies without relying on hardware locality constraints.
Optimize circuits with fast classical simulation to lower the estimated energy beyond the reported experiment.
evidence_signal: The authors state their method reproduces the largest Sci. Adv. 2025 experiment in under a minute on a laptop and achieves a lower ground-state energy than the experiment.
watch_item: The result applies to single-layer unitary cluster Jastrow circuits, so stronger or deeper circuit variants may not be covered by the same classical shortcut.
paper_title: Efficient classical simulation of large-scale unitary cluster Jastrow circuits
